subject: Third-party pen test: data exchange & runbook for ISV integrations
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lin <peter.lin@cyberlynx.com>, security@blueoak.io
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Third-party pen test: data exchange & runbook for ISV integrations

Peter / BlueOak team —

Thanks for agreeing to lead the external penetration test for our upcoming ISV integration wave. Attached is a working draft of the runbook for how we want to handle evidence exchange, temporary data access, and QA acceptance for integration partners. Key asks up front: 

- Confirm the minimum transport method you require (S3 presigned, SFTP, or on-site collector). We prefer encrypted S3 presigned URLs with limited lifetime.
- Confirm any credentials/hosts we will need to open to your scanners (IP ranges) and your standard scan windows.
- Clarify what types of artifacts you will need (logs, sample payloads, replayed traffic, API keys masked) so we can minimize PII exposure.
- Expected retention length for raw artifacts post-engagement (we propose 30 days).

I've highlighted two sections in the runbook: "evidence mux" (how to push artifacts to a redwood-controlled S3 bucket) and "data redaction" (recommended redaction patterns for customer PII). Chloe — can you confirm the service-side endpoints we will use for temporary buckets and whether we can auto-provision pre-signed uploads? Grace — flag anything in legal/compliance that would block a 30-day retention.

Proposed timeline: kickoff week of Dec 13, active testing Dec 20–24, validation Jan 4–8. If those dates work we'll lock the contract SOW and send DocuSign.

Attachments: redwood-3p-pentest-runbook-v0.9.pdf, data-exchange-matrix.xlsx

Best,
Monica Patel
Head of Partnerships (Security Integrations)
Redwood Inference
---

From: Peter Lin <peter.lin@cyberlynx.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security@blueoak.io
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Third-party pen test: data exchange & runbook for ISV integrations

Monica —

Thanks for the runbook draft. A few clarifications from the CyberLynx side: 

1) Transport: presigned S3 uploads are fine. We will request PUT-only presigned URLs with a 48-hour TTL for bulk artifacts, and GET-only presigned URLs for any artifacts we need to pull back in-house. We can support SFTP as a fallback.

2) IP ranges: our scanners originate from 34.210.55.0/24 and 18.198.34.0/24 (AWS); we also use an external proxy pool that may shift — we'll give you final CIDRs at least 72 hours before active testing.

3) Artifacts: we will request (a) replay packets for failing flow repros, (b) API request/response pairs (redacted tokens), (c) logs with timestamps. We do not need full customer datasets — sample payloads are fine. For any PII we request redaction rules (we can accept hashes for phone/email).

4) Retention: 30 days is acceptable with one caveat — we require a 90-day access window for any artifacts used in remediation verification if the customer has an open ticket. We can keep things encrypted and access-logged.

We also attached a short requirements doc (attached in-line). If legal wants to tighten retention we can add an amendment.

On timing: Dec 20–24 is tight for our team due to year-end scans. Suggest moving active testing window to Jan 3–7 and validation the week of Jan 17 to give both sides time to sign off.

—Peter
Senior Technical Director, Assessments
CyberLynx Security

Subject: Re: Third-party pen test: data exchange & runbook for ISV integrations

Folks —

Thanks Peter, that TTL approach works. Couple of implementation notes from infra/ops: 

- We can auto-provision pre-signed buckets scoped to an engagement id. Buckets will be encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys (tied to the engagement) and access logged to our audit trail.
- We'll expose a single endpoint for upload metadata POSTs (signed by the upload job) so we can validate checksums and run a redaction pass pre-ingest for common PII patterns. That redaction step is asynchronous and will leave a manifest in the bucket.
- For the 90-day access window ask: we can snapshot artifacts to a restricted archive class with strictly enforced RBAC and MFA to retrieve. Retrieval will generate an auditable event and require a remediation ticket ID.

Attached is a redline of the runbook with implementation annotations (redwood-3p-pentest-runbook-v0.9-redline.pdf). I'm calling out two required action items for your side: provide final CIDRs and confirm whether you need encrypted POST metadata (we can sign it).

If the timing shifts to Jan 3–7 we can schedule an infra dry-run the week prior (Dec 27–31) to validate provisioning scripts.

Chloe Martin
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Peter / BlueOak —

Great, thank you for the quick responses. Summary and next steps (mutual action plan):

1) Schedule: active testing window moved to Jan 3–7, 2027. Validation week Jan 17–21.
2) CIDRs: Peter to provide final CIDRs by Dec 22. Chloe to provision pre-signed buckets and send test pre-signed URL by Dec 27 (dry-run).
3) Retention: Redwood agrees to 30-day default retention with a 90-day restricted snapshot available if remediation ticket created. Legal will capture the snapshot flow in the SOW.
4) Artifacts & redaction: CyberLynx to request only sample payloads and logs; Redwood will run automated redaction and produce a manifest.
5) Contract: Monica to push SOW and DocuSign link by Dec 17; contracts@acme-corp.com will be looped in if we need procurement review for the ISV partner program.

Attachments: final runbook (redwood-3p-pentest-runbook-v1.0.pdf) added to the shared Drive link. I've also attached a short checklist for the partner onboarding team.

Peter — once you confirm the CIDRs I'll open the playlist for the dry-run. Thanks everyone — this looks like a clean path.

Best,
Monica Patel
Head of Partnerships (Security Integrations)
Redwood Inference
